title: Starter Choices & First-Run Survival
summary: Compare the three starters, learn movement and level-up choices, and decide when to work toward a fusion.

sections.title: Set up your first run
sections.text: The first useful goal is to reach a point where you can tell why you died. A death while boxed in, a boss you cannot damage, and a run lost while chasing a pickup are three different problems. They should lead to three different changes.
paragraphs: Open the original game, choose a Guest session if you are trying it out, and start with one of the three offered partners. This site does not share a save with the game. Before investing a long session, inspect the game’s account and save options so you know where your progress lives.

Keep the region, difficulty and partner the same for a few attempts. Changing all three makes it hard to learn anything from a better time. In the opening, pay attention to where enemies arrive, how your first attack reaches them, and which route remains open when a group closes in.
sections.caption: The original starter selection. Choose one of these three first; the other two can join your League after completing two runs.

sections.title: Choose between Bulbasaur, Squirtle and Charmander
sections.text: Bulbasaur, Squirtle and Charmander teach different habits. You do not need to reroll your account to find a perfect start. Pick the one whose passive helps with the problem you are actually having.
paragraphs: Bulbasaur is a sensible first choice when repeated small hits are draining your run. Synthesis adds regeneration and healing, and Grass hits provide small, capped healing. That rewards keeping attacks connected while you create space. It does not make standing inside a crowd safe.

Squirtle gives armor and shield immediately. That is useful when learning how much room a group needs and how far a projectile travels. Charmander’s Sea of Flames increases damage below 40% HP, with a separate Fire bonus. Treat that low-health bonus as help in a bad situation; deliberately sitting at low HP is a rough way to learn an unfamiliar arena.
rows: Synthesis: +1.5 regen and +25% healing. Your Grass attacks heal you a little (0.4% of HP per hit, up to 5 times per second).
Torrent Shell: +15 armor and +20 shield. Below 40% HP, +40% damage.
Sea of Flames: Below 40% HP, +40% damage. +10% Fire damage.
sections.callout: Species HP and run HP are different. These run baselines exclude passives, Lab and upgrades.

sections.title: Collect experience without getting surrounded
sections.text: Use the default controls deliberately: WASD moves, the mouse adjusts the camera, Space jumps, and Shift slides. Check the current controls menu if your bindings differ. Press Esc somewhere safe to inspect the pause menu before an unfamiliar decision.
paragraphs: Make a short loop around the outer edge of a group instead of reversing into the enemies you just passed. Look beyond the nearest pickup. A pocket of experience can be collected on the next circuit; a closed exit can end the run now. The useful question is whether you still have somewhere to go after taking it.

When you take repeated contact damage, spend the next attempt watching your route rather than watching damage numbers. If the route is open but projectiles keep landing, work on camera direction and lateral movement. If the same patch of ground is causing trouble, identify that hazard instead of assuming another armor level will solve it.

sections.title: Choose between moves, move levels and vitamins
sections.text: A new move takes a slot. A level in a move you already own improves that move. A vitamin changes stats and takes a vitamin slot. These are separate resources, so an attractive new attack can still be the wrong choice when it blocks a planned slot.
paragraphs: At each offer, ask what the run lacks. If enemies survive long enough to surround you, improving an attack that already connects may help more than adding another underleveled one. If you kill safely but lose health to occasional hits, a defensive or recovery choice can protect the damage you already have.

Read the actual damage class rather than guessing from the element. A Fire-looking kit is not permission to take every special-damage offer, and a physical opening does not mean every later move is physical. The Attacks list shows the damage class, shape and level growth used in PokeBonk.
steps: Identify whether the offer adds a move, raises a level or modifies a stat.
Check the slot it needs and the damage class it supports.
Choose one reason to take it. Do not change the entire build for one attractive card.

sections.title: When to start upgrading fusion ingredients
sections.text: Bill’s Machine can combine two eligible moves at level 8 or above and free a move slot. It is tempting to plan every first run around a named result, but acquiring the ingredients is only half the job: both need enough upgrades, and you need to survive until the machine is useful.
paragraphs: Learn what each ingredient does before reserving its slot for a fusion. Attacks includes all 106 fusion outcomes: 79 signature recipes, eight reactions, 18 same-type results and MissingNo. Open the intended result to check its ingredients and learners, then decide whether those ingredients can carry the current run.

A name alone is not enough to choose a pair. Signature recipes take priority over reactions and same-type results, so check the intended outcome before spending several upgrades. Confirm the machine preview in the run, especially after a patch changes attacks or recipes.

TM Case raises normal moves from level 8 to level 10 and lets a fusion grow from ★5 to ★6. You still only need level 8 on each ingredient to fuse. Do not hold back a useful fusion while waiting for level 10, and do not make finding this Legendary item a condition for a successful first run.
sections.caption: The League interface shows the kit, passive and progression. Check these before committing to a recipe.

sections.title: Review why your run ended
sections.text: After a run, make one short note: what stopped you, what your main damage source was, and what you will change. “Need a stronger build” is too broad. “Had no room to move after chasing experience” gives you something to practice immediately.
paragraphs: If you reached the same wall twice, inspect the Lab and locked League partners. An unlock challenge gives the next run a purpose even when a clear is still out of reach. Spend Stardust against the problem you observed; there is no need to buy the first affordable button just to leave with a purchase.

KOs, Survival and Time attack reward different things. The Global KO board adds regional bests, so playing another region can matter more than repeatedly improving one. Survival rewards time. Time attack compares completed regions before total time. Choose the mode after deciding what you want the next run to accomplish.
sections.callout: One partner, one setting, one build change, one note after each run. Try a new partner when you have a specific reason to want its passive.

sections.title: Favorites, Build Plan and guardian portals
sections.text: A Favorite is a selection shortcut, not a stat bonus. A Mastery Look is a cosmetic challenge reward. Most of its challenges also count in co-op; challenges that limit the number of hits you may take still require solo play. Pick your partner for its passive and opening kit, then choose a cosmetic independently.
paragraphs: The in-game Build Plan is useful once you have a specific pair in mind. Mark the attacks you want and watch for the planned-choice labels. Marking an attack or item does not unlock it, reserve an offer or add a move slot. If an item is locked or archived, fix that in the menu before expecting it in your next attempt.

After beating a guardian, the arrow and minimap guide you to its Great Ball and then the portal. In Lavender Tower’s Beyond, Bill’s Machine appears every three floors. If you are following an older walkthrough, check the current patch before assuming a missing machine or a changed menu means the run is broken.

seo.description: Choose a PokeBonk starter, survive the opening and make useful level-up choices. Learn movement, fusion basics and how to review what ended your last run.

title: PokéBonk Survival: Builds, Long Runs & Mewtwo
summary: Plan recovery, attack coverage and level-eight fusions for Survival, then review long-run risks and regional records.

sections.title: Survival is about keeping a build useful after the opening
sections.text: Survival is the game’s endless mode: open maps, continuing hordes and a run measured by how long you can stay alive. A comfortable first ten minutes is useful, but it is not evidence that the same damage and recovery will carry a long attempt. Treat the opening as a chance to assemble an engine, rather than the whole test.
paragraphs: The menu calls this mode Survival. Lavender Tower’s Floors of the Beyond are a separate event progression, not the same leaderboard. Check the mode before committing Bag supplies or setting an achievement target. If you want a specific reward, read its actual condition; a Classic clear, a Survival duration and a Tower floor are different results.
sections.callout: Survival and the Tower’s Floors of the Beyond are separate modes.

sections.title: Choose recovery you can keep triggering
sections.text: Bulbasaur is a useful starting point when small hits wear you down: its Grass-hit recovery rewards attacks that continue connecting while you move. That makes attack coverage part of your defense. If the crowd blocks your escape, however, a healing passive does not turn the middle of that crowd into a safe place.
paragraphs: Squirtle provides armor and shield, which makes early mistakes less punishing. Chansey is worth comparing when recovery is your limiting factor. These are recommendations for learning and consistency, not a claim that any one partner owns the longest-run record. A kit whose attack pattern you can aim and sustain may serve you better than a higher score in an opening-focused tier model.

Keep the same map, difficulty and partner while evaluating a change. If you change all three and last longer, you cannot tell whether the new item helped or the opening simply suited that partner. Use the pause panel to inspect the build you actually have, including the level-up modifiers on each move.

sections.title: Build damage and space at the same time
sections.text: A long run needs more than one attractive damage number. Ask whether your attacks reach the enemies that close your exits, whether they keep connecting while you move, and whether you can finish tougher targets before the next crowd removes your room. An attack that covers your escape route can be more useful than another underleveled attack with a large tooltip.
paragraphs: Match vitamins to the damage class listed for the move. An elemental theme does not guarantee that every attack in the kit uses the same class. In the current pause panel, inspect the combined level-up bonuses instead of comparing only level-one definitions. If coverage is already comfortable but tough enemies survive, invest in the attack doing the work before filling every empty slot.

sections.title: Plan a fusion without abandoning the current run
sections.text: Both eligible ingredients need level 8 at Bill’s Machine. That is a real investment in offers and slots. Pick a pair whose ingredients help before they fuse, and have a fallback if the second ingredient never arrives. Holding a weak move for a planned result can cost more health than the eventual fusion returns.
paragraphs: For Bulbasaur, compare Razor Leaf plus Solar Beam for Flower Beam. For Squirtle, Rapid Spin plus Hydro Pump gives Hydro Spiral. Check the fusion entries in Attacks for the exact pair and the resulting pattern. Signature pairs take priority over reactions and same-type outcomes; weather, buff and existing fusion patterns are not eligible ingredients.

Fusion stars and ordinary move levels use different limits. Fusion Star Shard adds one to the fusion-star cap, while the corresponding move and vitamin cap items have their own effects. Read the item and your current panel rather than assuming that every cap bonus raises everything by the same amount.

sections.title: Prepare for the 45-minute Mewtwo encounter
sections.text: The current game includes a Survival achievement for defeating Mewtwo at minute 45. Use that as a planning checkpoint, not an invitation to wait motionless until the clock changes. Before a major encounter, collect safely, identify the route you can keep moving through and check whether your main attacks still deal meaningful damage to durable targets.
paragraphs: During the fight, judge danger from the arena and telegraphs rather than the boss health bar alone. Losing a safe route to chase one pickup is a poor exchange when a long attempt is at stake. If damage stalls, note the attack classes, coverage and upgrade choices that got you there; repeating the same purchases with a different cosmetic does not answer that problem.

sections.title: Use migration and side activities when they improve your position
sections.text: Published Survival updates add migration portals, comets, regenerating altars, Ditto and Hypno. Their appearance is an opportunity to evaluate, not a requirement to cross a dangerous crowd. Keep a way back out of the interaction and decide what the run needs before spending time or resources on it.
paragraphs: A portal can change the situation you are playing in. Read its prompt and check your health and nearby enemies before committing. The game also distinguishes ordinary progression, seasonal challenges and cosmetic targets. For Mastery Looks, inspect the specific mode and objective. Most challenges can count in co-op now, but hit-limit challenges still require a solo run; a long Survival result is not automatically a Classic win.

sections.title: Keep a long session stable
sections.text: A long attempt also tests your browser. The official notes include performance work for Survival past 100 minutes, but that does not guarantee identical performance on every device. Choose settings that keep movement readable, close unrelated heavy tabs and notice sustained frame drops before they begin causing contact damage.
paragraphs: Before a long attempt, check the game’s account and save options. If performance becomes uneven, note when it starts and whether reducing effects restores readable movement. Record the mode, map, difficulty and game version alongside the attacks and items that worked; that makes the next attempt easier to compare without blaming every failure on the partner.

sections.title: Read the Survival ranking correctly
sections.text: The regional Survival record is your best duration on that map, with KOs breaking a tie. The Global board adds regional bests. Improving a weaker regional record can therefore matter more to your Global total than adding a few seconds to a region you have already pushed hard.
paragraphs: Our leaderboard keeps its capture date visible because rankings change. The personal tier board serves a different purpose again: it lets you record your own opinion of all 151 species. The editorial kit comparison emphasizes Classic openings and should be a shortlist for Survival experiments, not proof of late-run scaling.

sections.title: Review one limit before the next attempt
sections.text: After a run, write down the first problem you could not recover from: no escape route, insufficient damage on durable enemies, recovery that stopped triggering, or a device that could not keep up. Then choose one change. That might be a different attack, a defensive upgrade, a more useful fusion pair or lower graphics settings.
paragraphs: Check Lab costs before spending the Stardust you earned. Extra capacity helps only if you have useful offers to put in it; another damage level helps only if the attack can reach its target. Keep the next goal specific enough that you can tell whether the purchase helped when you reach the same point again.

title: PokéBonk Co-op: Rooms, Builds, Revives & Portals
summary: Set up a shared run, choose complementary kits, revive teammates and avoid outdated boss advice.

sections.title: Check access and agree on the run before readying up
sections.text: Co-op is a team run, not a solo attempt with extra spectators. Start in the game’s Co-op menu and check whether your account currently has access. The client supports invite-only and paused availability messages. If either appears, this guide cannot unlock the mode or override the server; follow the availability shown in the game.
paragraphs: Choose what the group is trying to do before anyone spends supplies: a first clear, a better regional time, or learning a particular encounter. A group split between exploring and rushing a record will make conflicting decisions even when every individual build is sensible. Keep the destination and difficulty visible while everyone confirms the plan.
sections.callout: Availability is controlled by the game. Co-op does not pause while you open menus.

sections.title: Set the room to a map everyone has unlocked
sections.text: The current room only permits maps and difficulties unlocked by the whole team, and identifies a player who does not have the selected destination. Resolve that before starting instead of assuming the host’s progress applies to everyone. The room also warns about version differences; a player on an older tab should update the game before another connection attempt.
paragraphs: Use the room link or the in-game invitation controls when your group is ready. Change your Pokémon through your own room card. Choose your Bag items in the lobby below the difficulty before readying up; they are consumed only if the match starts. Agree on whether these supplies serve the shared goal instead of spending them by habit. Check the final selection, map and difficulty once more, especially after someone leaves or joins. The Start flow waits for peer connections; repeated ready clicks do not repair a blocked connection.

sections.title: Pick complementary jobs without inventing an MMO party
sections.text: You do not need a rigid tank, healer and damage lineup to learn a map. Start with the failure you expect: enemies closing the route, a boss taking too long, or a teammate repeatedly losing health. Choose partners and attacks that address those problems, then check whether their useful effects actually benefit the team or only their owner.
paragraphs: Squirtle’s protection makes its own player more forgiving to pilot. Bulbasaur’s healing depends on its own attacks connecting. Neither passive is a reason to promise the group a universal taunt or a party-wide heal. Keep the actual move descriptions open when evaluating a support plan; a familiar Pokémon role from another game is not evidence of a mechanic here.

For a first clear, two players who stay alive and cover a route can be more useful than a fragile burst plan copied without its required upgrades. Once the group is consistent, compare what each player contributed and change one partner or attack choice at a time. The solo opening tier model is not a measured team-composition ranking.

sections.title: Keep a shared escape route
sections.text: Enemies chase nearby trainers, so movement changes which player is under pressure. Avoid dragging a crowd straight across the teammate who is already making room for an attack. Move around the edge of the danger and look at where the other players will need to go next, not only at your own nearest pickup.
paragraphs: Coordinate pickups and interactions when the area is crowded. Being in the same room does not remove the need to read telegraphs. If one player is taking repeated damage, ask whether the route, camera direction or chosen attack pattern is causing it before concluding that the group needs a completely different roster.

sections.title: Menus do not make the whole team safe
sections.text: Co-op does not pause when you open the pause menu: you remain exposed. The choosing player receives protection during an upgrade selection, but that player’s damage stops while choosing. A long decision therefore changes the pressure the rest of the team is handling. Read likely choices in advance and make the decision deliberately.
paragraphs: Keep a workable attack core rather than starting several underleveled projects at once. Bill’s Machine still requires eligible level-eight ingredients, so discuss a planned fusion before relying on it to solve the next boss. The correct question is whether the ingredients help your current team survive long enough to finish that plan.

sections.title: Revive by making room, then holding E
sections.text: Go beside a downed teammate and hold E to revive. The official notes give a one-minute revive window. Identify the safe approach before running directly through the enemies that downed them. If a second player falls while attempting a rescue, the team has traded one recoverable problem for two.
paragraphs: One surviving player can draw pressure away while another approaches the revive. That is a movement plan, not a guaranteed aggro-lock mechanic. Watch the actual enemy positions and be ready to adjust. Hold the interaction rather than repeatedly tapping it, and look for its progress before assuming a lagging response means you should abandon the rescue.
steps: Check the downed teammate’s position and the nearby crowd.
Create a safe approach; avoid bringing a second crowd to the rescue.
Stand beside the teammate and hold E while watching progress.
Regroup before returning to pickups or the next portal.

sections.title: Gather at the portal and ignore obsolete boss advice
sections.text: To move to the next zone, the team needs to be in the portal. It appears in the same place for everyone. If progression seems stuck, check who is still outside rather than searching for a different portal or immediately leaving the room. A player still collecting across the map can hold up the transition.
paragraphs: Version 0.8.46 removed the prior seal barriers, Wrath, shifting team weaknesses and linked elite pairs. Bosses and elites returned to fighting like their solo counterparts. Older videos can therefore describe mechanics that your current room no longer has. Judge the encounter in front of you and compare the patch version before following a specific old positioning script.

sections.title: Handle connection problems through the room
sections.text: Co-op needs browser peer-to-peer connections through WebRTC. If the game reports that these connections are blocked, use its troubleshooting message and compare a supported browser. Do not enter credentials into a site claiming it can unlock a room, and do not disable unrelated security protections just to test an invitation.
paragraphs: The official notes describe rejoining after a dropped connection and returning to the same room when a run ends. That is useful recovery behavior, not a promise that every interruption preserves every result. After reconnecting, confirm the shared map and team state before acting on what the screen showed before the disconnect.

sections.title: Choose a cosmetic goal the whole run can support
sections.text: The co-op leaderboard requires every team member to have an account. The game states that a co-op run also contributes to each player’s individual leaderboard, subject to its validity rules. A private planning board on this site cannot submit a team record or verify whether the server accepted a particular attempt.
paragraphs: Most Mastery Look challenges now count in co-op. A win means the team wins, but the other conditions still check your own actions: a teammate’s attack choice does not satisfy your move requirement. Challenges that allow at most a specified number of hits remain solo-only, so read the objective before inviting the group. These rules apply to completed runs under the updated system; do not expect an old attempt to be credited again. The shrine legendary’s shiny roll is also shared by the team: if it is shiny for one player, it is shiny for everyone. Finish the session with a specific next goal, whether that is safer revives, a cleaner portal transition or meeting your own move condition.

title: Best Pokemon in PokeBonk: Who Should You Choose?
summary: Choose a starter or your next unlocked partner with clear reasons, build directions and tradeoffs for Classic, Survival and co-op.

sections.title: Best Pokemon in PokeBonk: the quick answer
sections.text: For a fresh account, Bulbasaur is our first recommendation. Once more League partners are unlocked, Slowpoke leads our solo Classic opening comparison. Bulbasaur is available from the first-partner screen; Slowpoke requires an unlock and asks you to accept slower movement.
paragraphs: If several small mistakes usually end your run, choose recovery or control before chasing a larger damage number. If you survive comfortably but cannot clear a route, inspect the attack pattern and damage class of your kit. Those are different problems, and the same partner will not solve both equally well.

This guide uses the reviewed v0.8.62 kits and our Classic opening comparison: comfort receives 50% of the weight, offensive potential 30% and utility 20%, without Lab, vitamins or items. These are editorial scores, not measured win rates, timed boss tests or an official ranking.
rows: Grass-hit healing needs attacks to connect.
Slower movement makes late turns dangerous.
The recovery cast needs a charge ready.
Vines only stop four nearby enemies.
Armor and shield do not provide healing.

sections.title: Best starter: begin with Bulbasaur for recovery
sections.text: Synthesis grants +1.5 regeneration and +25% healing. Grass attacks also heal 0.4% HP per hit, capped at five triggers per second. Keep attacking while moving around the crowd rather than standing inside it to force another healing trigger.
paragraphs: Vine Whip starts equipped. Razor Leaf becomes a kit offer from run level 2, Sleep Powder from level 4 and Solar Beam from level 7. Offers are not automatically learned attacks. Give the opening enough investment to reach the later choices safely instead of saving every decision for a move you do not have.

Razor Leaf and Solar Beam form Flower Beam when both reach attack level 8 and you use Bill’s Machine. The signature uses special damage, so Calcium supports that route. Compare recovery or armor for the remaining vitamin slots when contact damage still gets through.

Bulbasaur reaches Ivysaur at run level 24 and Venusaur at 41. Those are run levels, not attack levels. Reaching Venusaur does not finish a fusion, and finishing Flower Beam does not replace the experience needed for evolution.

sections.title: When Squirtle or Charmander fits better
sections.text: Squirtle gives immediate protection through Torrent Shell: +15 armor and +20 shield, with +40% damage below 40% HP. That buffer helps while learning spacing. Our B-tier opening placement reflects what it lacks after the buffer is spent: built-in healing.
paragraphs: Water Gun starts the run. Bubble, Rapid Spin and Hydro Pump become later kit offers. Rapid Spin plus Hydro Pump forms the special-damage Hydro Spiral signature. Improve the attacks keeping your lane open now; do not leave the opening weak while waiting for Hydro Pump.

Charmander supplies +10% Fire damage and +40% damage below 40% HP through Sea of Flames. Fire Spin plus Flamethrower forms Fiery Whirlwind. The Fire bonus supports its kit, but deliberately staying at low HP leaves very little room for the next mistake.

Charmander’s C-tier position here describes opening comfort, not Charizard’s late-run damage ceiling. Squirtle reaches Wartortle at 24 and Blastoise at 44; Charmander reaches Charmeleon at 24 and Charizard at 44. Choose the starting kit that gets you there.
rows: Add recovery or a reliable escape route.
Protect health rather than forcing the low-HP bonus.

sections.title: Best unlocked pick for a forgiving opening: Slowpoke
sections.text: Slowpoke leads our comparison because recovery, a larger health pool and recurring sleep all help you reach the upgrades that make a run work. Its passive adds +25% HP and +1.5 regeneration, with -10% speed. Every 6 seconds, its yawn can put enemies within 6 metres to sleep.
paragraphs: That does not mean a permanently stopped horde. Use an interruption to correct a route and collect experience through a lane your attacks already cleared. The speed penalty makes early, broad turns more important than last-second reversals.

If you regularly wait until enemies close the gap before choosing a direction, Slowpoke can feel worse than a quicker partner below it in the list. Slowbro’s later armor bonus is also not protection you should count as already active in the opening.

Its League challenge is to put 8,000 Pokémon to sleep. If Slowpoke is locked, keep using an available partner; this recommendation is not a prerequisite for a clear. Complete the normal League challenge and capture process before planning a run around it.

sections.title: Clefairy and Tangela offer different recovery plans
sections.text: Clefairy adds +20 luck and +1 regeneration, charges the Ultimate 30% faster and recovers 15% HP when you cast it. Spend that reset while its healing matters instead of holding every charge for an imagined perfect boss moment.
paragraphs: Luck does not guarantee the next upgrade. A recently spent Ultimate leaves a gap, so ordinary attack coverage still has to protect you between casts. Its League challenge is to cast 80 Ultimates, giving you an unlock target while playing partners you already own.

Tangela adds +2 regeneration. Every 5 seconds, vines root and damage the four closest enemies within 7 metres. That helps against nearby pursuers, but four trapped enemies are not an entire stopped horde. Ranged threats outside that circle can still punish your route.

Tangela requires 20 League members and reaching level 35 in a run. It is a useful later recovery option, while Bulbasaur remains the immediate recommendation for a fresh account. Pick based on the tools you can actually bring into the next attempt.

sections.title: Why another tier list may rank damage picks higher
sections.text: A list that values completed final-form damage can order partners differently from one that values the opening. Read the comparison goal before copying its highest row. A kit that demands careful positioning can still be a good damage choice.
paragraphs: Machop’s +25% physical damage gives a clear build direction when the attacks you keep use physical damage. It does not improve a special signature just because that signature belongs to the same run. Its unlock challenge is to defeat 20 Alpha Pokémon.

Rhyhorn provides +15 armor and a charge after 1.5 seconds of uninterrupted running. It rewards broad movement rather than repeatedly stopping in a small pocket. Unlocking it requires 20 League members and smashing 100 rocks with Rock Smash.

Keep the region and difficulty fixed when trying another partner. Note whether you lost to chip damage, a closed lane or insufficient clearing. Changing the partner, Lab and route together makes it hard to tell which change helped.

sections.title: Choosing for Survival and co-op
sections.text: The Classic opening order is a shortlist for Survival, not a prediction of the strongest completed long-run build. Ask whether the kit can keep clearing, recover between difficult stretches and escape when enemies stop dying quickly.
paragraphs: Bulbasaur gives a concrete Survival direction through its Grass signature and hit-based recovery. It still needs usable ingredients before fusion. Slowpoke offers a recovery-oriented opening, but its movement penalty remains a positioning commitment even when its opening rank is high.

For co-op, choose with the room. Another damage pick may add little if the group already clears well but keeps losing players to poor routes. Stacking recovery-oriented kits also does not automatically supply missing attack reach or coverage.

Check the room’s unlocked map, difficulty and access before planning. Do not assume a passive describing your own healing also heals teammates. A useful team choice starts with understanding what the kit actually does, not assigning an unsupported healer or tank label.

sections.title: Choose your next partner in five decisions
sections.text: Use the partner you can select today, then make one attempt answer one question. Fixing a repeatable problem is more useful than changing characters whenever you find a different ranking.
steps: On the first-partner screen, try Bulbasaur for Grass-hit recovery or Squirtle for immediate protection.
If Slowpoke is unlocked and chip damage ends your runs, try its recovery while planning turns earlier.
When using Clefairy, cast the Ultimate while the healing matters rather than judging the kit without using it.
Choose a fusion whose ingredients work before they combine. Both need attack level 8 at Bill’s Machine.
After the run, identify the failure. Change partners if another kit addresses it; otherwise adjust movement or upgrades first.

sections.title: Questions before you choose
sections.text: What is the best Pokémon in PokeBonk overall? Slowpoke is our first unlocked pick for solo Classic opening comfort. For a fresh account choosing between the three starters, we recommend Bulbasaur. Neither answer promises the highest completed-build damage.
paragraphs: Is Charizard better than Venusaur? Compare Charmander’s Fire damage route with Bulbasaur’s Grass-hit recovery and decide which addresses your problem. They are later forms of different starting kits; species stat totals alone do not establish a universal winner.

Do you need a legendary Pokémon to clear? This recommendation does not require one. Get useful attacks working with an available partner and learn a repeatable route. A difficult unlock is not evidence that it will fix an early positioning mistake.

Are evolved forms separate starting partners? Not in these starter families. Choose Bulbasaur, Charmander or Squirtle and evolve during the run. The 151 Pokédex species and 79 League starting kits describe different things.
Is this an official ranking? No. It is our editorial comparison under the opening conditions stated above. No measured win rate, universal consensus or invented testing history is claimed.

title: PokeBonk Shiny Guide: Catching, Charm & Classic Looks
summary: Learn how to catch a shiny, unlock its family look and work toward Shiny Charm. Understand what stays saved and why a shiny catch may not unlock a partner.

seo.title: PokeBonk Shiny Guide - Catching, Charm & Unlocks
seo.description: Use this PokeBonk shiny guide to catch encounters, unlock family looks and earn Shiny Charm. Learn Classic Shiny differences and why a partner stays locked.
keywords: how to get shiny pokemon in pokebonk

sections.title: PokeBonk shiny: what you actually unlock
sections.text: A shiny catch can unlock a look for its evolution family, add to your collection and give you a companion during the run. It does not automatically recruit the normal starting partner into your League. That distinction explains the common situation where a shiny is recorded but the Pokémon is still locked.
paragraphs: Treat the encounter, the saved look and the selectable partner as three separate things. If you want to play the species from the start of a later run, complete its League challenge and capture the normal partner as well. If you only want to wear the shiny look, first check that the family has joined your League.

The numerical perks below use the reviewed v0.8.62 client records, checked October 28, 2026. Later patches can change encounter behavior. This guide does not turn an older number into a claim about the live version or promise a shiny after a fixed number of runs.

sections.title: Shiny, Classic Shiny and other Looks are different
sections.text: Read the encounter or wardrobe label rather than identifying every unusual colour as the same unlock. Classic Shiny is described by the game as the original shiny colours with classic sprites, appearing very rarely with a golden glow.
paragraphs: The ordinary Shiny label and Classic Shiny label are separate collection and appearance states. Catching a Classic Shiny unlocks the classic look for the evolution line once that partner is in your League. Do not assume an ordinary shiny automatically grants every appearance in the wardrobe.

Mastery Looks come from their stated challenges. Spectral and other appearances can share the same wardrobe with shiny options without sharing their unlock conditions. An unusual costume on a League card is not evidence that a wild shiny was captured.

sections.title: How to catch a shiny when one appears
sections.text: Make the encounter the priority as soon as you notice it, but reach it through an open lane. A rare target is not worth losing the run while running directly through a pack. The game has explicit messages for a shiny vanishing, so avoid spending its whole appearance window elsewhere.
paragraphs: Use the capture input displayed for your current controls. On keyboard, follow the game’s nearby capture prompt; on touch or controller, use the on-screen action instead of assuming a keyboard shortcut applies. Wait for the catch result before treating the shiny as secured.

The useful confirmation is a captured or look-unlocked message and the collection entry afterward. Simply defeating a target, spotting it in the Pokédex or being near a teammate’s catch is not a substitute for completing your own required interaction.
steps: Identify whether the prompt says Shiny or Classic Shiny so you know which collection state you are trying to unlock.
Clear a safe route to it and weaken the encounter until the game presents its capture state.
Move close and use the displayed capture action to throw your Poké Ball.
Wait for the game’s catch confirmation. Do not leave a target that is still waiting for a throw.
Afterward, check the League look or collection entry, and check normal recruitment separately.

sections.title: How to unlock Shiny Charm
sections.text: In the reviewed client, Shiny Charm is the six-shiny collection perk. Its description says shinies appear 50% more often and take 150 seconds to flee instead of 120. It is a collection milestone, not a Lab purchase named Research.
paragraphs: A 50% increase is relative to the underlying appearance rate. It does not mean half of all encounters are shiny, and the longer escape window does not guarantee a successful catch. Check the collection milestone shown in your current game before planning around the perk.

Use the collection’s own progress counter when checking whether you have reached the milestone. Do not assume every repeated catch, every alternate Look or every achievement increments the same counter. The rewards table is not an invitation to substitute achievement catch totals for collection progress.

sections.title: Shiny collection rewards worth working toward
sections.text: The collection gives more than a different colour. The reviewed client lists the following permanent milestones. Check the threshold inside the collection, then decide whether another capture is the goal for this attempt rather than changing every part of your build at once.
rows: Shinies appear 50% more often and take 150 s to flee (was 120 s).
Your shiny partner joins with Bond 2 (+20% damage).

sections.title: Can you improve your shiny chances?
sections.text: Shiny Charm is a confirmed appearance-frequency perk in the reviewed data. The Bag also has a consumable named Dawn Stone whose description guarantees a shiny appearance in zone 1. An appearance guarantee is not a catch guarantee, and it does not say you can choose the species or force a Classic Shiny.
paragraphs: Check the exact item description before spending Stardust. The reviewed Bag record calls its icon shiny-stone, while the separate in-run Dawn Stone catalogue item describes damage and attack-speed bonuses. Similar names and shared artwork do not mean those items perform the same job.

The Master Ball found as an in-run item says it guarantees capture in Wild Encounters. That is a different job from causing an encounter to appear. Do not combine the Bag Master Ball’s separately worded first-capture effect with the item’s effect and assume every future throw is guaranteed.

Base shiny odds are not quoted here because they need a current, mode-specific check of the encounter logic. In particular, a chance rolled once per zone is not a chance on every enemy defeated. Avoid converting a percentage from another game or a different patch into an expected number of kills.

sections.title: After the catch: equip the look and manage your companion
sections.text: Return to the League or its Looks selection and inspect the family you caught. If the normal partner is already recruited, choose the unlocked shiny appearance there. If it is still locked, complete its normal challenge and capture first; the shiny look can wait for that recruitment.
paragraphs: The recorded replacement prompt allows one shiny companion at a time. When another shiny is caught, read which Pokémon the interface is asking you to release. The game’s message says you keep the Pokédex entry and the stated Stardust either way, so releasing the companion is not the same as deleting the collection entry.

A companion leaving the current run and a saved family look are different states. Before reporting a lost shiny, check the correct Shiny or Classic Shiny view and the family’s normal League status. Also keep using the same account or saved session; this fan site cannot read or restore the game’s save.

sections.title: Why your shiny Pokémon is still locked
sections.text: The game explicitly separates a shiny catch from a normal League capture. If you caught a shiny Bulbasaur after choosing Charmander, for example, you have not necessarily completed Bulbasaur’s normal recruitment. Check its challenge, complete it and catch the normal partner when it appears.
paragraphs: The same distinction applies to evolved forms. A shiny Charizard appearance belongs to the evolution family; it does not make Charizard a separate level-1 starting partner. Start with the recruited Charmander and follow the run’s evolution path to use its later forms.

Do not erase your save just because a wardrobe option and a locked League card appear together. Read the locked card’s requirement and confirm whether you have a normal catch, a shiny look, or an Alpha companion that only fought alongside you in one run.

sections.title: Co-op catches and shiny legendaries
sections.text: Co-op capture instructions tell each player to throw their own Poké Ball after the team weakens an eligible encounter. Follow your own prompt instead of assuming another player’s interaction completed yours.
paragraphs: The reviewed update text says a legendary’s shiny roll is shared by the team. That describes the shared roll, not an instruction to skip the encounter or the required capture interaction. It also does not establish that all ordinary shiny encounters have the same shared-roll rule.

If a selected mode says captures are disabled, use a mode that permits them for your collection goal. A reliable hunting attempt starts by checking that the run can actually award the thing you are seeking.

sections.title: PokeBonk shiny FAQ
sections.text: Does a shiny make the Pokémon stronger? Equipping a shiny look is described as cosmetic. Collection perks and the shiny companion’s Bond reward are separate benefits; a different colour alone is not an extra damage stat.
paragraphs: Can a shiny run away? Yes. The game has vanished messages for both Shiny and Classic Shiny, and the reviewed Charm description extends the escape time. Get to the encounter promptly and finish the capture rather than relying on the extra time.

Does Shiny Charm guarantee Classic Shiny? No guarantee of a Classic Shiny is stated in the reviewed perk description. Do not interpret more frequent shinies as a promise about a particular variant or species.

Does replacing my shiny companion remove the look? The replacement prompt says you retain the Pokédex entry and stated Stardust. Check your saved collection and wardrobe separately from the current companion slot.

Is there a guaranteed shiny farming route? The reviewed Bag Dawn Stone describes a guaranteed appearance in zone 1. That does not establish a repeatable route for a chosen species, a guaranteed capture or an unlimited free farming method.
